container_info.description: A native application that allows users to create, edit, and manage notes locally on their device.
container_info.reasoning: The Application Description specifies a native application for creating, editing, and managing notes locally on the device. 'native' is explicitly provided in the Framework field and must be used per the detection rules. A notes app that stores and edits content locally aligns with desktop (Windows/Mac/Linux GUI) platform-type rather than web or mobile. The container image is a development helper with many SDKs and CLIs preinstalled, but the app description and 'native' framework indicate a local GUI native client.
alternative_frameworks: Electron (for cross-platform desktop using web tech)
Tauri (lightweight desktop apps with Rust + web front-end)
React Native (for cross-platform if targeting mobile/desktop via extensions)
requirements: OS packages: minimal build-essential, git, curl (already present in container)
Runtime: choose one depending on chosen native toolchain (e.g., Node.js + npm for Electron/Tauri frontend; Python3 for PyQt/PySide; dotnet-sdk-8.0 for .NET MAUI/WinForms/WPF if targeting .NET)
Headless build tools: npm or yarn (for Electron/Tauri), python3-pip (for PyQt), dotnet CLI (for .NET) — only the runtime/CLI needed to build and run locally
Core dependencies: minimal framework package (e.g., electron package via npm install --save-dev electron OR python packages pyqt5/pyqt6 via pip OR dotnet workload for desktop), no optional plugins
Storage: file-based storage (no external DB); use local filesystem or SQLite for persistent notes
Testing: lightweight unit test runner for chosen stack (jest for JS, pytest for Python, dotnet test for .NET) with a minimal sample test

Headless configuration: environment variables for non-GUI builds (e.g., BUILD_TARGET=linux), CI-friendly build scripts (npm scripts, python setup.py or simple Makefile, dotnet build), and Xvfb only if GUI tests must run headless
Build output: simple artifact packaging step (electron-builder for Electron if needed) but optional for development — focus on 'npm run start' / 'python -m' / 'dotnet run' commands
Avoid: heavy DB servers, caching systems, production monitoring, optional plugins or extensive native installers

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Persist minimal system-wide environment for development and validate Node/npm availability. Writes NODE_ENV=development and BUILD_TARGET=linux to /etc/profile.d so future shells see them and ensures the workspace directory exists. Validates preinstalled node (>=18) and npm (>=9).
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/local-notes-manager-292529-292550/notes_native_client"
SHPATH="/etc/profile.d/notes_native_client.sh"
NODE_V_RAW=$(node -v 2>/dev/null || true)
NPM_V_RAW=$(npm -v 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$NODE_V_RAW" ] || [ -z "$NPM_V_RAW" ]; then echo "node/npm not found; container must provide node and npm" >&2; exit 2; fi
NODE_MAJOR=${NODE_V_RAW#v}; NODE_MAJOR=${NODE_MAJOR%%.*}
NPM_MAJOR=${NPM_V_RAW%%.*}
if [ "${NODE_MAJOR:-0}" -lt 18 ]; then echo "node >=18 required (found $NODE_V_RAW)" >&2; exit 3; fi
if [ "${NPM_MAJOR:-0}" -lt 9 ]; then echo "npm >=9 required (found $NPM_V_RAW)" >&2; exit 4; fi
sudo tee "$SHPATH" > /dev/null <<'EOF'
# notes_native_client development environment
export NODE_ENV=development
export BUILD_TARGET=linux
EOF
sudo chmod 644 "$SHPATH"
. "$SHPATH"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"

steps.name: project scaffolding
steps.description: Deterministically create or repair a minimal Electron project in the authoritative workspace. Back up any existing package.json (safe), initialize package.json if missing, merge minimal scripts and pinned dependencies/devDependencies without overwriting existing versions. Create src files (main.js, index.html, storage.js using sqlite3), jest.config.js, a lightweight Jest test, and .gitignore. Ensures package.json is present for subsequent steps.

steps.name: install dependencies
steps.description: Install Node dependencies in the workspace non-interactively. Prefer npm ci when package-lock.json exists; if it fails, fall back to npm install. Export PYTHON to help node-gyp. After install verify node_modules and local binaries exist; if sqlite3 failed to build provide a clear remediation recommending libsqlite3-dev. Create package-lock.json if missing to stabilize subsequent runs.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/local-notes-manager-292529-292550/notes_native_client"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
if [ ! -f package.json ]; then echo "package.json missing; run scaffold-001" >&2; exit 2; fi
export PYTHON=$(command -v python3 || true)
if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
  if ! npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --prefer-offline --silent; then
    echo "npm ci failed; falling back to npm install" >&2; npm install --no-audit --no-fund --silent; fi
else
  npm install --no-audit --no-fund --silent || true
  if [ ! -f package-lock.json ]; then npm i --package-lock-only --silent || true; fi
fi
# verify node_modules and local binaries
if [ ! -d node_modules ]; then echo "dependency install incomplete; node_modules missing" >&2; exit 10; fi
if [ ! -x ./node_modules/.bin/jest ]; then echo "local jest binary missing: ./node_modules/.bin/jest" >&2; exit 11; fi
if [ ! -x ./node_modules/.bin/electron ]; then echo "local electron binary missing: ./node_modules/.bin/electron" >&2; exit 12; fi
# sqlite3 native build remediation
if grep -q '"sqlite3"' package.json 2>/dev/null; then
  if [ ! -d node_modules/sqlite3 ] && [ ! -f node_modules/sqlite3/package.json ]; then
    echo "ERROR: sqlite3 native binding did not install cleanly. Remediation: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libsqlite3-dev" >&2; exit 13
  fi
fi

steps.name: scaffold repair and reinstall
steps.description: Recovery step invoked when tests fail due to missing package.json or broken install. Recreate/repair package.json by re-running scaffold-001 and then reinstall dependencies (deps-001). This enables autonomous recovery from the engineer's observed blocking failure.

steps.name: start
steps.description: Start the Electron app via 'npm run start' in the workspace for interactive VNC sessions. Ensures DISPLAY is set (defaults to :99), sets container-friendly Electron flags (ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX=1) for headless operation, verifies package.json start script exists, and starts the app in background.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/local-notes-manager-292529-292550/notes_native_client"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-:99}
export ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=1

if [ ! -f package.json ]; then echo "package.json missing; run scaffold-001" >&2; exit 2; fi
node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); if(!p.scripts||!p.scripts.start){console.error('package.json missing start script'); process.exit(2);}"

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Validate build and start of the Electron app headlessly. Depends on env-001, scaffold-001, deps-001, test-001 and start-001. Optionally runs npm run build (non-fatal), starts the app, watches logs for readiness markers and tears down the process cleanly, providing log evidence.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/local-notes-manager-292529-292550/notes_native_client"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export DISPLAY=${DISPLAY:-:99}
export ELECTRON_ENABLE_LOGGING=1
export ELECTRON_NO_SANDBOX=1
if [ ! -f package.json ]; then echo "package.json missing; cannot validate" >&2; exit 2; fi
# optional build (non-fatal)
if node -e "const p=require('./package.json'); process.exit(p.scripts&&p.scripts.build?0:0)" 2>/dev/null; then
  npm run build --silent || true
fi
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-/tmp}
LOG="$LOG_DIR/notes_native_client.log"
rm -f "$LOG"
# start via npm script so local electron is used
npm run start --silent >"$LOG" 2>&1 &
EPID=$!
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= -p $EPID 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)
READY=0
for i in {1..30}; do
  if grep -q "renderer up" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null || grep -q "App is running" "$LOG" 2>/dev/null; then READY=1; break; fi
  if ! ps -p $EPID >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "start process exited prematurely" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true; exit 21; fi
  sleep 1
done
if [ "$READY" -ne 1 ]; then echo "app did not signal readiness within timeout" >&2; tail -n 200 "$LOG" || true; PG=${PGID:-$EPID}; kill -TERM -"$PG" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 2; kill -KILL -"$PG" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; exit 22; fi
echo "APP_PID=${EPID} PGID=${PGID}"
head -n 80 "$LOG" || true
PG=${PGID:-$EPID}; kill -TERM -"$PG" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; sleep 2; if ps -p $EPID >/dev/null 2>&1; then kill -KILL -"$PG" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi
echo "validation completed"

The plan enforces environment persistence (NODE_ENV, BUILD_TARGET) via /etc/profile.d, creates a deterministic Electron project scaffold in the authoritative workspace, installs dependencies non-interactively preferring npm ci, runs lightweight unit tests with local Jest, and validates by starting the app headlessly against the existing X server at DISPLAY=:99.
